To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) XAFS is a very powerful method for determining the local structure of nanoparticles and nanowires; (ii) XEOL is a powerful technique for determining the electronic structure of nanoparticles and the local structure of nanowires, while XES provides information on the local structure of the nanowires; and (iii) TRXEOL is a powerful tool for determining the kinetics of the formation and decay of excited states in nanowires.

the electronic structure and optical absorption of nanoparticles and nanowires of materials such as gold, silicon, germanium, diamond, zinc sulfide, cadmium sulfide and related materials are significantly different from those of the bulk.

(1) the local structure of metal and semiconductor nanoparticles can be probed with high precision using EXAFS and XEOL spectroscopy and (2) the optical properties of nanowires of semiconductor materials can be probed using synchroton X-ray emission spectroscopies, which include X-ray excited optical and electronic luminescence spectroscopy and X-ray emission spectrscopy, and the results are interpreted in terms of the electronic structure of the materials.
